newsitem.title: USA: CME hog and pork belly futures expected lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hog and pork belly futures expected lower.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open 0.100 to 0.300 cent a lb lower while pork belly futures were called 0.250 to 0.500 cent a lb lower, livestock analysts said.

Carryover selling from the second consecutive day of limit losses in October and sharp declines in other months were expected to weigh on hog futures early. The weak tone to technicals and declines in cash hog prices should add to pressure, they said.
Pork cutout values have been slipping, prompting packers to bid lower for cash hogs. Also, hog marketings have been adequate and could increase as expected wet weather arrives at midweek, they added.

The recent greater-than-expected slaughter pace and sliding cash belly prices were expected to keep pessure on pork belly futures, especially after the sharply lower to limit down close in bellies Monday, sources said. The market also looks technically very weak after falling to its lowest level since May 31.
Technically, futures could go down to the 64 to 66 cent-a-lb area based on the close under 72 cents Monday, they said.
The CME said its out-of-town belly report will be delayed until Wednesday due to the holiday on Monday.
